{{short description|Human resources company based in Dublin}} {{multiple issues| {{Self-published|date=June 2019}} {{more citations needed|date=June 2019}} {{Update|date=June 2019}} }} {{Use dmy dates|date=July 2015}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=July 2015}} {{Infobox company | name = CPL Resources | type = [[Public company|Public]] | traded_as = {{unbulleted list|{{EuronextDublin|DQ5|IE0007214426}}|{{AIM|CPS}}}} | logo = CPL Logo.jpg | logo_size = 160px | founded = 1992 | hq_location = [[Dublin]], Ireland | area_served = Europe | key_people = {{ubl|[[Anne Heraty]] ([[Organizational founder|founder]])|Paul Carrol (business development)| Lorna Conn ([[Chief Executive Officer | CEO]]) | Josephine Tierney ([[Chief Financial Officer|CFO]])}} | industry = Human resources | revenue = {{ubl|€ 212,4 million (2009)| € 257,6 million (2008)}} | net_income = {{ubl|€ 43.000 (2009)| € 17,6 million (2008)}} | website = https://www.cpl.com/ie }} '''CPL Resources''' is a [[human resources]] company based in [[Dublin]] that operates in Ireland and Europe. It was founded in 1992. CPL was founded by [[Anne Heraty]] and Keith O'Malley as Computer Placement Ltd in 1989. Currently, the group has 12 companies spread over 21 offices: 12 in the Republic of Ireland, two in Northern Ireland, and seven in the rest of Europe. == Description == As of 2010, CPL consisted of 12 companies with 21 offices (excluding the place of work at the premises of CPL's customers):Overview Specialist Areas on Investor Relations website] {{Cite web |url=http://investor.cpljobs.com/specialist_areas.html |title=Specialist Areas |access-date=2 June 2010 |archive-date=16 June 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100616001141/http://investor.cpljobs.com/specialist_areas.html |url-status=dead }}, visited 2 June 2010 * CPL: IT, construction, sales/marketing, call-centers (using companies and/or trade-names as: CPL Resourcing, CPL Solutions, CPL Engineering etc.) * Careers Register – Finance, accounting, banking and insurance * Tech Skills – Engineering and construction * ThornShaw – Pharmaceutical & Medical Devices * Flexsource – Industrial, Manufacturing, Hotel & Catering, Retail, Logistics, Construction and Warehousing * Ardlinn – Executive Search consultancy specializing in senior appointments (€100,000+) {{cite web| url = https://www.ardlinn.com| title = Global Irish Executive Search {{!}} Ardlinn}} * Clinical Professionals Group – Europe's leading life science recruiter *Covalen – Managed Services, Outsourcing, Consulting & Advisory Services. == History == In 1989, Anne Heraty and Keith O'Malley founded Computer Placement Ltd. providing staff for the IT industry. In 1992, Heraty bought out the other shareholders, including O'Malley and became the 100% owner of CPL. In 1996, Heraty's husband Paul Carrol joined the company. Currently, he is the director of Business Development. In 1994, a restructuring of Computer Placement Ltd. started and from then on they used CPL mainly as a trade-name. The restructuring continued over the next few years and in 1996 the companies' CPL Engineering (construction) and CPL Solutions (IT/call centres) were founded. In 1997 the first new office opened in [[Limerick]]. In 1998, some new divisions were set up within Computer Placement Ltd: CPL Telecoms, CPL Sales and CPL Financial.[http://investor.cpljobs.com/history_of_cpl.html History of CPL] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100616001125/http://investor.cpljobs.com/history_of_cpl.html |date=16 June 2010 }} on investor relations website of the company, last visited 3 June 2010 In July 2018, a [[Channel 4]] investigation on ''[[Dispatches (TV programme)|Dispatches]]'' titled ''Inside Facebook: Secrets of a Social Network'' described CPL's role in providing [[content moderation]] services to [[Facebook]] through a team of employees who were instructed to allow certain types of [[graphic violence]] and [[hate speech]] to remain on Facebook.{{refn|{{cite web|first1=Nick|last1=Statt|access-date=2019-06-21|title=Undercover Facebook moderator was instructed not to remove fringe groups or hate speech|url=https://www.theverge.com/2018/7/17/17582152/facebook-channel-4-undercover-investigation-content-moderation|date=17 July 2018|website=[[The Verge]]}}{{cite news|first1=Michael|last1=Hogan|access-date=2019-06-21|title=Inside Facebook: Secrets of the Social Network, review - Reveals disturbing posts that Facebook allows on its site|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/tv/2018/07/17/inside-facebook-secrets-social-network-revealed-disturbing-posts/|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|date=17 July 2018|issn=0307-1235}}{{cite web|first1=Isobel Asher|last1=Hamilton|access-date=2019-06-21|title=Secretly filmed footage reveals the training Facebook moderators are put through|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/facebook-moderator-training-secretly-filmed-by-channel-4-2018-7|website=[[Business Insider]]|date=18 Jul 2018}}{{cite news|first1=Colin|last1=Gleeson|access-date=2019-06-21|title=CPL has 'strong relationship' with Facebook despite Channel 4 documentary|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/business/technology/cpl-has-strong-relationship-with-facebook-despite-channel-4-documentary-1.3672144|newspaper=[[The Irish Times]]|date=23 Oct 2018}}}} In March 2019, a former worker at CPL's [[Dublin]] location reported a high-pressure environment where moderators were required to evaluate videos containing graphic violence, [[child pornography]], [[animal abuse]], and other disturbing content with the expectation of meeting a 98% "quality rating".{{cite news|first1=Jennifer|last1=O'Connell|access-date=2019-06-21|title=Facebook's dirty work in Ireland: 'I had to watch footage of a person being beaten to death'|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/culture/tv-radio-web/facebook-s-dirty-work-in-ireland-i-had-to-watch-footage-of-a-person-being-beaten-to-death-1.3841743|newspaper=[[The Irish Times]]|date=30 Mar 2019}} == Mergers and acquisitions == CPL has acquired over a dozen companies during its existence.
